title: Simplify browser form protection while retaining necessary tokens
goal: Remove token setup only from form paths that can use automatic cross-origin checks, while preserving token-dependent browsers, custom data and compliance defenses.

selectionNotes: RC2 behavior: automatic SSR/Minimal API and explicitly opted-in MVC; Razor Pages retains its token filter.

packageAssets: Matching Microsoft.AspNetCore.App shared framework and Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Internal.Assets; CsrfProtectionMiddleware is automatically wired by WebApplication.CreateBuilder
providers: Default ICsrfProtection; built-in antiforgery/Data Protection; PermitAdditionalData in retained-token mode
platforms: ASP.NET Core server; modern browser with Fetch Metadata or Origin; actual Windows x64 Chrome 155 and loopback HTTP
renderingModes: Razor Pages with retained token filter
prerequisites: Use every listed file in standalone QuayPermits. Preserve Pages/Permit.cshtml's first @page directive. Empty Directory files isolate parent build/package configuration. Restore matching framework assets before offline builds.
constraints: Default automatic verdict is enforced at protected form consumers. SSR and form-bound Minimal APIs work without token middleware; MVC must opt in with RequireAntiforgeryToken in this RC2 artifact. ValidateAntiForgeryToken remains a token filter; do not combine both attributes. Razor Pages retains tokens because its automatic filter still demands them.

Retain AddAntiforgery/UseAntiforgery, form/cookie token pairs and IAntiforgeryAdditionalDataProvider when older browsers, additional token data or compliance require token defense. The sample --keep-tokens true does so; --reject-additional true is a deliberate negative control. RC2 token middleware can overwrite the automatic verdict, so coexistence is not proof of two independent enforced layers.

JSON endpoints are unchanged. Headerless non-browser requests are allowed by automatic protection; do not mistake this for authentication. Neither token defense nor CORS replaces authorization, input validation or HTTPS. The sample stores no application data and implements no authentication.

Only explicit credentialed CORS trust is accepted: /trusted permits http://localhost:6019 with AllowCredentials. Wildcard or public-read policies do not grant CSRF trust. Do not opt browser/cookie endpoints out with DisableAntiforgery or IgnoreAntiforgeryToken merely to suppress a rejection.
optIns: MVC RequireAntiforgeryToken; retain --keep-tokens true for token-dependent consumers
stabilityLimitations: Stable API designation with RC2 artifact-specific evidence. Current migration prose overstates the tested MVC legacy-filter/Razor Pages integration; GA reconciliation remains required.
